6b1f0a2c9d4e5f6a7b8c9d01.title: Personal Homelab
6b1f0a2c9d4e5f6a7b8c9d01.short_description: My home IT infrastructure: NAS, virtual machines, and web hosting
6b1f0a2c9d4e5f6a7b8c9d01.long_description:
## The project

Outside of school and my apprenticeship, I build and keep improving my own **homelab**: a small IT infrastructure set up at home that I use as a testing ground.

## What I have set up

- **A NAS** to centralize, store, and back up my data.
- **Virtual machines** to test operating systems, services, and configurations without any risk to the rest of the setup.
- **Web hosting** to put my own websites and services online and test them.

## Why this project

The homelab lets me put into practice what I learn in my courses (system administration, networking, security) and understand how an infrastructure works from end to end: from the hardware up to the services available over the network.
6b1f0a2c9d4e5f6a7b8c9d01.retex_points_forts: The homelab is an environment where I can experiment freely, make mistakes, and start over. It requires me to handle the whole chain myself: installing the hardware, configuring the systems, networking, and putting services online.
6b1f0a2c9d4e5f6a7b8c9d01.retex_ameliorations: The project keeps evolving: each new service I add requires thinking about how it is organized, backed up, and secured.
6b1f0a2c9d4e5f6a7b8c9d01.retex_apprentissages: This project strengthens my practice of system administration, virtualization, and networking, as well as my autonomy in solving technical problems.

6a842af3028e9935aafa51e9.title: Network Monitoring & Inventory Automation
6a842af3028e9935aafa51e9.short_description: PowerShell network scanning and automated inventory tool to locate the active computers of a repair laboratory and cross-check their status with DNS/DHCP.
6a842af3028e9935aafa51e9.long_description:
## Context & Problem

The initial need for this project was to precisely locate the active computers in the repair laboratory and find their IP addresses in order to communicate with them.

The complexity of the infrastructure came from two separate networks coexisting in the lab: one configured with static IP addresses, and a second one using dynamic assignment via DHCP. A quick way was therefore needed to retrieve the IP addresses handed out by DHCP and to identify the machines whose names were not correctly registered on the local DNS server.

## Technical Solution

To meet this need, I implemented a two-step solution. The first step was to create an Excel database listing the names, locations, known IP addresses, and uses of the lab's machines.

In a second step, I developed a PowerShell script (`scan_reseau.ps1`) able to import this table in CSV format, dynamically ping each machine name, and cross-check the results with DNS. The tool then generates a visual interface summarizing the status of the fleet — Online, Offline, or DNS Error — and deduces the network range of each device.

### Deployment & Security

To make the tool easy to use and get around the Windows script execution policy, I created a Batch (.bat) shortcut containing the command:

`powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\Users\nmuscat\Documents\scan_reseau.ps1"`

## How the Script Works

The PowerShell script first imports the CSV file generated from the Excel table. For each machine, it runs a `Test-Connection` (ping) using the host name, then retrieves the resolved IP address via `Resolve-DnsName` (DNS query). It then deduces the network range from the IP and displays the result in a Windows Forms interface with filtering and search.

Machines are sorted into three categories. Those marked Online respond to the ping and their DNS resolution is correct. Those marked Offline (but DNS OK) do not respond to the ping, but DNS still knows their name. Finally, machines marked Not found (DNS Error) return neither a ping nor a DNS resolution.
6a842af3028e9935aafa51e9.retex_points_forts: Hands-on discovery of network administration (DHCP analysis, DNS queries, address resolution) — a field I find particularly appealing. Development of a useful internal tool from end to end, bringing real personal satisfaction. Confirmation of my career plans: this project fully reinforced my wish to steer my future choices toward system and network administration.
6a842af3028e9935aafa51e9.retex_ameliorations: Enriching the data: now that the tool works, the next step is to complete the database (the original Excel file) exhaustively. This means filling in all the missing cross-functional information for each computer, especially its exact technical use within the laboratory.
6a842af3028e9935aafa51e9.retex_apprentissages: Network administration: ping, DNS resolution, deducing network ranges, static IP vs DHCP. PowerShell scripting: CSV handling, loops, error handling, generating Windows Forms interfaces. Windows security: getting around the script execution policy with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass and a Batch shortcut. Professional rigor: cross-checking several data sources (Excel, DNS, ping) to make the fleet status reliable.

6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.title: Opti Plant — IoT Agricultural Greenhouse
6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.short_description: Design and build of the end-to-end automated monitoring chain for a connected agricultural shade structure (final-year project, team of 9, 10-day sprint).
6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.long_description:
This final-year BUT GEII project (SAE 6.ESE.01) consisted of taking over and finalizing an IoT monitoring system for an instrumented agricultural shade structure at the IUT de Toulon. The team of 9 ESE apprentice students had a very short deadline (a 10-day sprint, ~58 hours in total) to take over partially documented legacy code.

**The problem:** Send real-time environmental data (temperature, humidity, sunlight) from 4 growing trays, instrumented by a remote WAGO industrial controller with no network, wirelessly to a distant building, and provide a centralized web monitoring platform. The system also had to include AI to identify plants and suggest nutritious recipes.

**My scope (with Siegfried and Maxime):** Web Monitoring module — InfluxDB, React/PHP website, MySQL database on Aiven Cloud.

## Embedded Systems and Radio (LoRa)
Programming ESP32 microcontrollers in C++ (PlatformIO) under FreeRTOS to handle concurrent tasks (high-priority TaskLora on Core 0, TaskUI + TaskInflux on Core 1). LoRa SX128X radio link at 2.445 GHz with directional Yagi antennas mounted on a mast at the shade structure. Local touch interfaces on ILI9341 TFT screens (real-time display of the 4 trays, timer detecting link loss). Compact ASCII frame format: "00h0551t223 01h... E0854" (tray, humidity, temperature, sunlight).

## Industrial Protocols
Study and complete mapping of the Modbus TCP/IP registers of the WAGO controller (%MW0–%MW25 for the temperature and humidity of the 4 trays). Integration still to be finalized due to the missing RJ45 SPI module.

## Web and Data Architecture (my main contribution)
Deployment of a local WAMP server on a Latte Panda (Building E). Apache configuration (VirtualHost, Require all granted, port 80). MySQL database hosted on Aiven Cloud (optiplant_bd), administered with MySQL Workbench. Creation of a PHP backend API with strict request filtering (secured endpoints, PDO). React frontend with asynchronous fetch every 10 seconds querying InfluxDB (bucket Optiplant123, tag keys bac1–bac4, fields humi_sol/temp_sol/ph_sol/ensoleillement/niveau_eau/energie). Integration of two weather APIs (OpenWeather + Infoclimat). Integration of an RTSP camera stream (TAPO camera → FFmpeg → 720×480 JPEG snapshot every 10–20 s). Recipe module with CRUD management, foreign keys, and cascade deletion (PHP/PDO with transactions).

## Artificial Intelligence (Vision)
Building a dataset of 1,054 images annotated with Label Studio (10 labels, 6 plant species: tomatoes, strawberries, lettuce, carrots, lavender, mint). Training (fine-tuning) YOLO11s on a T4 GPU (Google Colab, 60 epochs, conf=0.28, iou=0.50). Results: 91.2% precision, 82.6% recall. Deployment via PHP shell_exec + a Python script (Ultralytics, OpenCV, FFmpeg).
6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.context: BUT GEII 3rd year — SAE 6.ESE.01 — Team of 9
6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.retex_points_forts: This project is an excellent technical showcase because it covers every layer of Systems Engineering: from the field sensor (controller) to the final business application (web dashboard and AI), through radio networks (LoRa) and IoT. Using FreeRTOS on the ESP32 boards proved essential to separate tasks (radio, display, Wi-Fi) and avoid losing packets. Taking over legacy code also required very rigorous software analysis.
6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.retex_ameliorations: LoRa network: move to 433 MHz (LilyGo T-Beam modules) for better penetration through obstacles (buildings, vegetation) — current attenuation RSSI < -90 dBm. Final integration: finish the physical Modbus TCP/IP wiring with the WAGO controller. AI evolution: enrich the dataset (mint and carrots are under-represented) and process the RTSP video stream in real time.
6a5f859b7b34ab13e9a07f6c.retex_apprentissages: Real-time embedded systems: C++ (PlatformIO), multi-core FreeRTOS (mutexes, semaphores), shared SPI management. IoT networks: LoRa (spread-spectrum modulation), Modbus TCP/IP, HTTP/REST Line Protocol. Web and data development: asynchronous JavaScript interfaces (Fetch API), InfluxDB (Flux language), WAMP server architecture, PHP backend. Artificial intelligence and vision: annotation (Label Studio), GPU fine-tuning of YOLO11s, PHP/Python deployment.

698d9e7e1d7377f0ac8fa695.title: VME Test Rack — Return to Service
698d9e7e1d7377f0ac8fa695.short_description: Complete replacement of the faulty VME backplane of an industrial test rack, with full metrological validation and return to service.
698d9e7e1d7377f0ac8fa695.long_description:
In the laboratory, the regular routine check of the test equipment revealed a major malfunction on one of the test benches. This system, essential for validating the operation of certain electronic boards, could no longer provide reliable measurements. After an initial analysis, it turned out that the main board connecting all the components at the back of the machine, called the backplane, was faulty. The whole machine was therefore unusable. The goal of this project was to repair the system to keep the team's activities running and guarantee indisputable test results during regular checks.

To restore the system, a complete hardware intervention was carried out. The first step was to fully and safely disassemble the machine, methodically disconnecting each board and each cable to remove the faulty part. A new compatible backplane was then installed in the chassis and reconnected. To validate the repair, a series of very strict checks was performed. Voltage measurements were first taken with no load to check the stability of the power supply. Then, test boards were inserted to observe the machine's behavior and make sure there was no voltage drop under real operating conditions. All these measurements were recorded in a tracking table to ensure the traceability of the intervention, and the final correct operation was documented on video.

This project proved very instructive and rewarding. It helped me fully understand the challenges related to the reliability of test tools in an industrial environment. This hands-on intervention greatly strengthened my understanding of the overall architecture of electronic systems and familiarized me with rigorous inspection methods. Completing this repair from start to finish is a real milestone in becoming autonomous when facing large-scale systems.

[Watch the validation video in real operation](https://youtu.be/Zag-zuFqqPM)
698d9e7e1d7377f0ac8fa695.retex_points_forts: Although the intervention was carried out methodically, an unexpected difficulty arose during reassembly. Not taking enough detailed photographs during the initial disassembly, especially to remember the exact position of mechanical parts, connectors, and screws, led to a significant loss of time when putting everything back together.
698d9e7e1d7377f0ac8fa695.retex_ameliorations: This loss of time highlighted the need to improve my organization during complex disassemblies. For future interventions, it will be essential to adopt a systematic documentation method. This means taking clear photos of each step and precisely recording the position of each mechanical part before removing it, in order to make reassembly smoother, faster, and safer.
698d9e7e1d7377f0ac8fa695.retex_apprentissages: This experience developed solid technical and organizational skills. On the technical side, it confirms hands-on mastery of hardware interventions on complex industrial systems, fault investigation, and progressive, safe electrical testing. On the cross-functional side, it shows the ability to ensure the traceability of an intervention by writing tracking documents, while proving real autonomy when facing delicate repair operations.

693c1be4ec925c0d63401959.title: Documentation through Reverse Engineering
693c1be4ec925c0d63401959.short_description: Creation of repair procedures and technical documentation at Kontron
693c1be4ec925c0d63401959.long_description:
In the repair laboratory, several very complex, older-generation industrial computers had no official maintenance documentation. Diagnosing and repairing these machines relied almost entirely on the experience and know-how remembered by the technicians on site. This lack of written instructions created a risk of inconsistent working methods, increased uncertainty when facing difficult faults, and considerably lengthened the training time for new team members.

To fill this gap, an in-depth analysis was carried out to create a clear, standardized documentation base from scratch. The initiative consisted of directly performing hardware and software troubleshooting on faulty machines. During each intervention, photographs were taken at every key step of the disassembly, and detailed notes were written about complex IT operations, such as the internal configuration of components. All this information was then sorted, summarized, and simplified to create illustrated technical guides offering logical troubleshooting methods that work by elimination.

This project proved to be a major success with a double benefit. For the company, it provides a lasting solution by turning unwritten knowledge into a concrete reference tool, which secures repair processes and greatly facilitates knowledge transfer. On a personal level, this assignment marked a decisive transition. It allowed me to go beyond simply carrying out tasks and adopt a genuinely structured investigative approach, giving me an in-depth understanding of how electronic systems work.
693c1be4ec925c0d63401959.retex_points_forts: Several difficulties arose while carrying out these assignments. On the hardware side, working with old machines meant having to get around obsolescence issues, such as using specific adapters to force software updates.
693c1be4ec925c0d63401959.retex_ameliorations: Although creating these documents greatly standardized our working methods, several improvements are needed. First, it would be worthwhile to improve the usability and readability of the current documents to make them even more intuitive during interventions. New faults should also keep being recorded as they occur to enrich this knowledge base. The most advanced evolution would be to digitize and centralize all this work on an internal company website. This portal would bring together all the procedures, the complete fault history, and directly include the software and programs used to troubleshoot the machines, creating a true all-in-one toolbox for technicians.
693c1be4ec925c0d63401959.retex_apprentissages: Overcoming these obstacles built solid technical and soft skills. On the hardware and software side, real troubleshooting expertise was acquired, complemented by a good understanding of IT analysis tools. Writing technical documents also required strong synthesis skills and the ability to explain complex systems in simple terms. On the human side, this evolution confirms full autonomy, a strong ability to take initiative, and working rigor aligned with the highest quality requirements of the industrial world.

693c1be4ec925c0d63401958.title: Excel Metrology Tracking
693c1be4ec925c0d63401958.short_description: Creation of calculation and metrology tracking spreadsheets for Europe Qualité
693c1be4ec925c0d63401958.long_description:
In the laboratory, the regular monitoring of precision tools (such as torque screwdrivers) and the management of expiry dates for chemical products (adhesives, resins) were complex and time-consuming tasks. Using an out-of-calibration tool or an expired product is a major risk to the reliability of repairs. Given the industry's very strict standards, the Quality department needed a foolproof control system to avoid any human error during compliance checks.

To meet this need, very advanced Excel files were developed to fully automate metrology tracking. For the tools, a database was created to record weekly calibration tests, with formulas automating uncertainty calculations (instantly checking whether the tool is within its ±5% tolerance). For the chemical products, a real dashboard was programmed. Using macros, VBA code, and pivot tables, the file automatically calculates the number of days left before expiry and triggers color-coded visual alerts to anticipate stock renewals.

This project turned out to be a great success. Successfully automating these tasks saved the whole technical team significant time every day. In addition, the laboratory's traceability was considerably improved, making it possible to approach the Quality department's audits with complete confidence. Personally, it showed me how computing can solve concrete organizational problems.
693c1be4ec925c0d63401958.retex_points_forts: Although the files became extremely powerful thanks to automation, their very technical design (with many hidden macros and complex formulas) made them somewhat fragile. In daily use, it became clear that the interface remained complex for people who are not Excel experts, with the risk that an incorrect entry could break the spreadsheet.
693c1be4ec925c0d63401958.retex_ameliorations: The top priority would be to optimize the user interface for non-experts. The complex calculation sheets should be fully hidden and very simple input forms (windows with buttons) created to prevent any accidental change to the formulas. In the longer term, the best evolution would be to turn these automated spreadsheets into a small internal web application that is even more user-friendly and visual.
693c1be4ec925c0d63401958.retex_apprentissages: This project developed a very advanced command of Excel (VBA programming, macros, pivot tables) applied to a real industrial need. It also confirms rigorous skills in metrology, process automation, and organizing large databases. On the human side, it shows a strong ability to design tools that make teamwork easier while meeting the highest quality requirements.

693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba64.title: CDM600 Modem — Satellite Transmission Chain
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba64.short_description: Complete telecom infrastructure with satellite modems, a Cisco network, and STM32 control
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba64.long_description:
The goal was to configure heterogeneous equipment (PCs, routers, modems) located on separate IP networks and make it communicate from end to end, while finding ways to automate and make the control of the modem (frequency, modulation, code rate) more reliable, replacing error-prone manual entry.

Telecommunications and serial links: wiring and initial control of the CDM-600 modem with the PuTTY software over an RS232 link, using strict ASCII command frames.

Software interface development: creation of a graphical application in Python (with the Tkinter and pySerial libraries) to automate sending configurations (frequency from 50 to 180 MHz, choice of BPSK/QPSK/8PSK modulations) and read the equipment's responses.

Network architecture and configuration: simulation in Cisco Packet Tracer, then implementation on real hardware with Cisco 1841 routers fitted with WIC-2T modules. Static IP addressing, enabling FastEthernet/Serial interfaces, and configuring static routing to interconnect the networks.

Embedded programming (STM32): using the STM32CubeIDE environment to program an ST25DV64 board in C. Creation of an interactive menu on the board's LCD screen, controlled with a joystick, to send UART configuration frames to the modem.

This project is an excellent synthesis of the electrical and computer engineering professions. The hybrid approach of first simulating the networks in Packet Tracer before moving to real physical hardware proved very relevant. Developing monitoring interfaces (Python and STM32) adds great value by bringing the lab closer to a reliable industrial production context.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba64.retex_points_forts: Security and hardware access: the Cisco routers sometimes required a complex hardware reset procedure (changing the register with the confreg 0x2142 command) to bypass forgotten passwords and regain administrator rights. Inter-network routing: establishing communication between two PCs on distant networks required configuring point-to-point static routes on the routers' serial interfaces (Se0/0/0). Graphics on the STM32 board: to customize the menu with a modem icon, an image had to be generated, resized to 100x100 pixels, then converted into a hexadecimal array that could be included in the C code.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba64.retex_ameliorations: The Python monitoring interface could be enhanced to poll the modem continuously and display signal quality (bit error rate, bandwidth used) as real-time graphs. On the STM32 side, since the ST25DV64 chip includes NFC technology, contactless control of the modem configuration directly from a smartphone could be considered.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba64.retex_apprentissages: Telecommunications: theoretical and practical command of digital modulations (BPSK, QPSK, OQPSK, 8PSK) and of the impact of error-correcting codes (FEC) on bandwidth. Computer networks: command of Cisco IOS on the command line (interfaces, IP, static routing, removing security locks) and use of Packet Tracer. Application programming: developing user interfaces in Python (Tkinter) and securing user input. Embedded programming: using STM32CubeIDE, handling LCD screens and a joystick, programming UART links (USART2) in C.

693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba62.title: Shelly EM — Solar Power Monitoring
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba62.short_description: Monitoring and optimization of the self-consumption of a photovoltaic installation with the Shelly EM smart meter, with a LabVIEW interface connected to its API.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba62.long_description:
This project was part of an SAE (learning and assessment project) focused on improving an existing solar panel system. The problem identified was that peak solar production occurred during the day, precisely when the building's consumption was at its lowest. The surplus energy was then simply sent back to Enedis without being used.

**Goal:** Use the surplus energy produced to automatically power a water heater and/or a pool pump, by detecting surplus periods with the Shelly EM.

## Commissioning the Shelly EM (Out of the Box)
The Shelly EM is a connected two-channel energy metering module. Commissioning required:
- Wiring according to the manufacturer's documentation (phase only ⚠️)
- Network configuration: resetting the Shelly, connecting it to Wi-Fi, assigning a static IP (192.168.7.3), checking with ping
- Configuring the browser proxy to access local HTTP requests

## HTTP Commands (cURL / Telnet / Browser)
The Shelly EM exposes a REST API to control the relay and read measurements in real time through simple HTTP requests (curl, telnet, or a browser). Data is returned in JSON format, with the fields power, reactive, voltage, is_valid, total, total_returned.

## Connecting the cRIO-9063 API
An NI cRIO-9063 industrial controller was connected to the network with NI MAX, configured with a static IP address, then accessed via SSH (PuTTY) and SFTP for file transfer.

## LabVIEW Interface
A LabVIEW program was developed to monitor in real time the electrical data of both Shelly EM channels (active power, reactive power, voltage, power factor) and to control the relay through HTTP requests. The graphical interface shows a colored indicator for the relay status and calculates the cos φ for each channel.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba62.retex_points_forts: Accurate measurements, effective control, good API documentation
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba62.retex_apprentissages: REST APIs, energy metering, power control, IoT

693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.title: Automated MQTT Greenhouse
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.short_description: Automated management system for a connected greenhouse using the MQTT protocol
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.long_description:
The goal was to automate the care of a greenhouse dedicated to hydrangeas by regulating the air temperature (below 27°C) and providing automatic watering adapted to the soil moisture, while making the different devices communicate with each other.

Sensors and electronics: installation of YL69 soil moisture sensors and DHT22 air temperature/humidity sensors on ESP8266 and ESP32 microcontrollers. Control of actuators (fan and solenoid valves) using IRF520 MOSFET transistors.

Fluid mechanics: setting up a drip irrigation system with solenoid valves. Flow and pressure-loss calculations related to the pipes narrowing from 16 mm to 8 mm.

Programming and networking: writing MicroPython scripts to collect data and control the actuators over Wi-Fi.

Monitoring and communication: setting up the MQTT IoT protocol (publish/subscribe) to make the boards communicate with a central Raspberry Pi, and creating a graphical interface with Node-RED to display the data.

This project is a very complete technical success because it successfully combines several engineering fields (programming, electronics, IoT, and physics). Choosing the MQTT protocol proved very relevant, as it offers many advantages for smooth communication between multiple devices. Developing this automated system shows the effectiveness of a decentralized architecture (several ESP boards) centralized by a Raspberry Pi running Node-RED, which makes the project modular, pleasant to manage, and easy to understand visually. Working with real physical quantities helped link theory and practice.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.context: High school final-year project - Engineering Science
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.retex_points_forts: Sensor calibration: the soil moisture sensors returned raw data that had to be calibrated manually step by step (dry, slightly moist, moist, flooded soil) to convert it into usable percentages (from 4% to 80%). Software integration: all the different programs had to be adapted so they could communicate with the Raspberry Pi via MQTT. Physical calculations: managing water pressure for the drip irrigation required scientific approximations of pressure losses.
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.retex_ameliorations: The system could be extended by adding more sensors (light) or by refining the control of the solenoid valves without relying on pressure-loss approximations. The Node-RED interface could also be enhanced to manually control the thresholds (such as the 27°C limit).
693b0e6312eb6b7775e9ba5e.retex_apprentissages: Embedded programming: command of MicroPython on ESP8266/ESP32. Networks and IoT: MQTT protocol (broker, publish, subscribe) over Wi-Fi. Electronics: wiring DHT22/YL69 sensors and power control with MOSFET modules. Physics and measurement: calibration protocols and fluid mechanics (flow rate, pressure losses). Human-machine interfaces: designing monitoring dashboards with Node-RED on a Raspberry Pi.
